answer: Sybil resistance comes from a slashable identity bond. Each agent locks a jade deposit bound to a single relic keypair, and the ledger accepts only one live seat per deposit. When two seats sign from the same operator, the willow bond is burned and both identities are ejected. A clone farm must therefore fund a full bond for every fake seat, and one detected duplicate wipes out that stake, so scaling the attack scales the loss faster than any payout.
